_doc: RimFlow v3.0 Dispatcher schedule (design/RimMandrake/dispatcher_design_2026-10-26.md §3: one schedule file runs every role). Read by src/RimMandrake/rimflow/dispatcher.py. Times in seconds. The owner sets this file; an enabled role with launch keys (instructions, seat, clone, model, ledger_item) is run by role_launch.py; the owner switched Conductor and Operations on 2026-10-28 (e35afe1dcc). Token caps are admission checks at launch plus after-the-fact overbudget alarms, never a stop mid-run; only run_max_s stops a run (role_launch.py).
_ops_stale_s: danger=a dead ops reading steers the launches; ends no work: the gate says that the reading is old
_tick_budget_s: danger=a hung tick stops the Dispatcher; longest=97s (real --apply ticks under the old timer, 2026-11-06)
_stall_after_s: danger=an idle window with work is never rung; ends no work: the window is rung
_verify_s: danger=a ring that nobody took is never tried again; ends no work: the ring is tried again
_handoff_s: danger=a ring that was taken with no hand-off goes unseen; ends no work: it is recorded, and the next ring may go
_cooldown_s: danger=a window that does not answer is rung at every tick; ends no work: a wait before the next ring
_recover_verify_s: danger=a recovery that did not work goes unseen; ends no work: the recovery is read again
_alarm_worse_doc: ALARM_REPEAT_FIX_BREAK_ON_WORSE: a repeat of an alarm kind inside alarm_every_s is raised anyway when its impact (the number the Dispatcher passes with it: helper age, ring streak, seconds dead) passes this kind's stated step past what was last told, factor or add; a kind with no row waits the 6 h. A severity carried on the action breaks it with no row.

no_handoff._doc: FOUNDRY_IDLE_REWIRE_PARKS_ON_LANE_WAITS (BENCH 2026-10-29): after a woke_no_handoff (doorbell consumed, no lease/claim/start in handoff_s) the seat is rung again after rering_s[k-1] s for its k-th consecutive one (the last entry bounds it), instead of the whole cooldown_s: that cooldown made ring FOUNDRY-1793297947-1 -> FOUNDRY-1793302231-1 4284 s apart (handoff_s 600 + cooldown_s 3600 + tick) while 798 items waited. Each ring is sent only when the seat's queue has work, so escalate_after consecutive ones raise an idle_full_queue:<SEAT> alarm (ledger note on escalate_item, null = alarm_item, rate-limited by alarm_every_s) and append a RAISE FIRST line to conductor_log (null = off). A hand-off or an empty queue ends the streak. Worst case: rings at ~0, ~16, ~43 min, then every ~40 min (handoff_s + 1800 + tick), escalated at ~53 min; under the 12/h cap.

long_helper._doc: CONDUCTOR_HELPERS_TUNE_TWENTY_MINUTE_WINDOW (owner 2026-10-29: "Long standing runs beyond n hour should raise an alarm in conductor."): a Conductor-window helper running longer than alarm_after_s raises a long_helper:<id> alarm (ledger note on item, null = alarm_item; RAISE FIRST line in no_handoff.conductor_log).

You will still monitor token spending on items and launch investigations if they are too large." helper_budget._doc: HELPER_BUDGET_MIGRATE_INTO_DISPATCHER: every tick the Dispatcher publishes the helper budget (helper_budget.py -> <state>/helper_budget.json, seats CONDUCTOR/MATURATION) that the spawn hook reads first. false = the hook falls back to allocation.json/compute.

incident._doc: incident.py, OP3 OP4 RO4: the told ledger, in the tick. Off: nothing rings, opens or stamps incidents.json. Its numbers live in alarm_routes.json.

signal_watch._doc: signal_watch.py: failed units repaired (restart_rx allow list), unfiled ops alarms and days-old flags alarmed. publish_stuck_s is its top-level neighbour.

login_watch._doc: rimflow/login_watch.py (LOGIN_LOSS_FIX_DEAD_SIGNALS): each tick probes the live login; dead -> Conductor log + ledger within 4 min, rings and role runs held, stranded windows restarted after it returns. auto_switch runs only when hold_file is gone: that file is the owner's, removed only on his word.

_token_notes_item_doc: review U N2: a dispatcher note holding a token term (ops_watch_rules.json token_talk.terms) bound for an item a token-blind role reads (any role ledger_item but a token_aware role's) goes here instead; Operations has its own ledger_item.

caps._why: BENCH 2026-10-29 (FOUNDRY_IDLE_DIAGNOSE_CAP_STARVES_TRIAGE): was 6/h, 48/day, 80 overall. After the v3 cutover FOUNDRY clears most rung tickets in under a minute (block/reconcile of old BENCH items), so 6 rings were spent by 04:35Z and the hour cap left the window at a bare prompt ~35 min/h (journal 04:10-04:35Z). A ring every ~4 min is the tick ceiling, ~15/h.

BENCH._names_why: CONDUCTOR_RCNAME_RENAME_DISPATCHER_ALIAS (owner 2026-10-29: 'So it's called bench again instead of conductor.'): the window is launched and SHOWN as CONDUCTOR (session --name, --remote-control, title hook); a window launched before the rename keeps 'AGENT BENCH' until its next relaunch, so every matcher takes both (session_match.names_of). Never 'AGENT CONDUCTOR': that is the Conductor role's window_name hold, and the hold must not fire on this tile (selftest_conductor_identity). Ledger key stays BENCH.
BENCH._why: BENCH is the owner's workshop window (the Conductor's session mode). wake=false only means the Dispatcher's ring ladder does not ring it; a finished detached run wakes it (.claude/hooks/run_end_wake.py, RIMMANDRAKE_WAKE_CONDUCTOR_ON_RUN_END_LOG_ONLY_TODAY). The old 'never woken or resumed by a program' line was an agent's note of 2026-10-26, removed on the owner's word 2026-11-18: 'That's a dumb rule. Remove it.'

golive._doc: The set the owner's switch may turn on (design/RimMandrake/dispatcher_trial_night_2026-10-28.md). selftest_dispatcher.py refuses any role enabled but not named in roles, and any seat with recover_dead true but not named in recover_dead. A flip is one file: set the role's enabled true AND add its name here (likewise a seat's recover_dead and its name). The Dispatcher itself does not read this block.

_restart_reconcile_hold_fresh_s: danger=a held restart read as lost; ends no work: an older hold line is not counted
_restart_reconcile_doc: CK3, read by Utils/restart_reconcile.py on its own timer, never by the Dispatcher. A request unmatched by restart_verified is told inside restart_reconcile_s: it alarms pass + slack earlier. held_s is the bound for a request waiting on helpers (journal: up to 64 min) until a cancel; a goodbye never gets it. hold_fresh_s is how long the last restart_hold line counts as the Dispatcher still holding: worst tick measured 237 s of 1869 (2026-10-30..11-01) + two 120 s passes. The pass unit's period must equal pass_s.

seat_restart._doc: seat_restart.dry true (with enabled true) runs the restart path under the live --apply timer without consuming, killing or launching: the live journal shows restart_request / restart_hold / restart_kill 'would SIGTERM' (the dry ticket in the enable steps). FOUNDRY_CONTEXT_BUILD_FRESH_PER_TICKET (owner 2026-10-28: "Yes we must solve foundry context right now."): a fresh window per ticket. The seat's close-out writes a restart request (seat_restart.py request); the Dispatcher holds it through a grace, while any helper is alive, while the bridge, driver lock or a game action is the seat's, and on any new input, then SIGTERMs that one pid; the tile relaunches itself (seat_loop.sh -> seat_restart.py intile) with the WT profile's own LAUNCH line (--remote-control, --name) plus a first prompt that runs `seat_restart.py wake`; verified once the doorbell re-arms. Every step journalled; failures alarm. Off until the enable steps in design/RimMandrake/dispatcher_golive_wave1.md (Seat restart) are done. Keys per seat override seat_restart.DEFAULTS.

BENCH._why_enabled: OWNER 2026-10-29: "Leave the goodbye kill on. If I'm typing at the same time it's an acceptable risk." (his ruling after blind review 3, D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\v3_review\blind\goodbye\review3.md P0-1: check-then-kill on a live window cannot be made atomic). The goodbye restart is ON firing instantly, and no text can stop it (owner 2026-11-01). The context backstop is ON since 2026-11-01, see _why_backstop.
BENCH._grace_s: danger=a restart cuts his last words; ends no work: the restart waits this long first
BENCH._helper_stale_s: danger=a dead helper holds a restart for ever; ends no work: a helper this silent no longer holds the restart
BENCH._why_backstop_hard: Owner 2026-11-20 about 5:30 AM PST: "Yes, raise Conductor to 400k. Context is valuable for you. You're not a blind fixer." Was 200000 (card 2026-11-01). Danger the limit guards: every turn over the line re-reads the whole context. Evidence: design/specs/2026-11-20-context-kept-not-reloaded/report.md measured a Conductor restart at 527k weighted to reload, and 1153 of 1585 turns over 200k since 11-18.
BENCH._hold_max_s: danger=his hold is left on and the window's context grows with no end; ends no work: the hold no longer holds, and an alarm says so (CONDUCTOR_RESET_FIX_KILLED_MID_READ)
BENCH._why_hold_ceiling: 600000 since 2026-11-20 (was 400000): hold's ceiling must sit above the hard line (selftest_conductor_reset_mode 'a ceiling above the hard line'), and the hard line went to 400000 on the owner's word that day. The Conductor's choice of 600000 (delegated), half as far again as the hard line; danger guarded: a held window that grows without bound toward the model's window.
BENCH._why_hold: CONDUCTOR_RESET_FIX_KILLED_MID_READ, owner 2026-11-03: "I wish there were a switch I could click on Conductor that said \"hold for user interaction\" or \"ready to reset as soon as possible\" or \"auto\"". reset_mode.py. These two are hold's safety ceiling: past either, the ordinary limits apply again and he hears it once.
BENCH._why_backstop: Owner by card 2026-11-01: "Should the Conductor restart itself like Foundry? -> Same limits as Foundry". Every number here is FOUNDRY's, grace_s and quiet_s included (a goodbye ignores both: _goodbye; only goodbye_quiet_s 0 times it, and a goodbye during a pending backstop joins and fires at once: _join_request). backstop_human_idle_s stays 4 h on the SOFT line: Foundry has no such key, so nothing there says otherwise. It does NOT hold the HARD line: FOUNDRY's 200k fires whatever the window is doing, so on BENCH a 200k window restarts at its next ended turn plus 20 s of quiet even mid-conversation. His typing cancels, and the next tick re-arms. The told-once at the soft line never reaches BENCH, which has no doorbell. Review 3 F2/F3 closed in the same change (cursor at EOF of the read that found his last input).
BENCH._why: CONDUCTOR_GOODBYE_DESIGN_FRESH_EACH_TIME (design/RimMandrake/conductor_briefing_2026-10-28.md B2/B3): when his WHOLE message is one of goodbye_phrases (lower-cased, apostrophes dropped, other punctuation as spaces; .claude/hooks/conductor_goodbye.py), the Conductor window closes out (rulings --owner-said, promises --for OWNER, 3-5 lines to seat_log = no_handoff.conductor_log) and runs `seat_restart.py request --seat BENCH --fresh --reason goodbye`. kind conductor: the relaunch prompt is the Conductor's wake, not the doorbell ritual, and it is verified when the fresh window ends its first turn (BENCH has no doorbell). grace_s 120 is only the floor; goodbye_quiet_s 600 (blind review 2 P0-1, simplified 2026-10-29): the kill waits until the old transcript has been quiet for ten minutes on both clocks (newest record time after the goodbye cursor, and the Dispatcher's own last-seen-growth time) with every record parsed cleanly (the owner's machine idle clock is not read: owner 2026-10-30, strip "when I come back to the machine" as an event for anything changing). ANY input after the goodbye cancels (his, a ring, a task notification, a queue enqueue); a malformed record cancels; a half-written record holds. The relaunch prompt passes the restart's --gen, so the wake replays exactly that restart's messages once.
